q: The experienced auditor test in SA 230 requires documentation sufficient to enable an experienced auditor with no previous connection with the audit to understand:
o: Every conversation held with management over the course of the audit
The commercial terms of the audit engagement and the basis of the fee
The nature, timing and extent of procedures, results and conclusions
The internal quality control policies operated by the audit firm
why: The test focuses on the audit work itself, its results, and the significant judgements and conclusions drawn. Fee arrangements and firm level quality control policies are not what the experienced auditor test addresses.

q: Under SA 230 the assembly of the final audit file should be completed on a timely basis after the date of the auditor report, ordinarily not more than:
o: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days
why: SA 230 indicates that an appropriate time limit for assembling the final audit file is ordinarily not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor report. The 60 day period is the assembly deadline and is distinct from the minimum retention period.

q: The retention period for audit engagement documentation under the relevant quality control requirements is ordinarily no shorter than:
o: Seven years from the date of the auditor report or group report
Five years from the date on which the auditor report was signed
Ten years from the balance sheet date of the financial statements
Three years from the date the audit file assembly was completed
why: Retention should ordinarily be no shorter than seven years from the date of the auditor report, or the group auditor report where later. Confusing this with the sixty day assembly period is a frequent error.

q: After the date of the auditor report but before file assembly is complete, the auditor deletes superseded draft workpapers. This is:
o: Prohibited in all cases, as nothing may be removed after the report date
Permissible, since assembly is administrative and adds no new conclusions
Permissible only with the written approval of those charged with governance
Permissible only if the deletion is disclosed within the auditor report
why: During the assembly period the auditor may perform administrative tasks such as deleting superseded drafts and sorting papers, because these do not change audit conclusions. What is prohibited is deleting or discarding documentation of substance before the retention period ends.

q: The auditor performs a new procedure after the date of the auditor report in response to a query from a regulator. SA 230 requires documentation of:
o: Only the additional procedure that was performed for the regulator
The name of the regulator and the fee charged for the additional work
A revised auditor report reflecting the additional work performed
The reasons, when and by whom made and reviewed, and the conclusions
why: When documentation is added after the report date, SA 230 requires recording the reasons, the who and when of the change and its review, and the additional procedures and conclusions. Merely filing the new procedure without this trail defeats the audit trail requirement.

q: Which statement about written representations under SA 580 is CORRECT?
o: Written representations are sufficient appropriate evidence on their own
Written representations are evidence but never sufficient by themselves
Written representations remove the need to test management estimates
Written representations may be dated at any point in the assembly period
why: SA 580 is explicit that representations are evidence but never sufficient on their own for the matters they address. They also cannot substitute for other evidence the auditor could reasonably expect to be available.

q: Under SA 580, written representations should be dated:
o: As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor report
On the balance sheet date to which the audited financial statements relate
Within sixty days after the date on which the auditor report is dated
On the date the financial statements are approved by the shareholders
why: The representations must cover all periods referred to in the report and be dated as near as practicable to but not after the date of the auditor report. Dating them after the report would leave the intervening period uncovered.

q: Management refuses to provide the written representation regarding its responsibility for the preparation of the financial statements. The auditor should:
o: Issue a qualified opinion and describe the refusal in the basis section
Obtain an oral representation from management instead and document it
Withdraw the audit report that has already been issued to the members
Disclaim an opinion, since all other representations become unreliable
why: Refusal of the fundamental representations about managements responsibilities undermines the reliability of all representations, so SA 580 requires a disclaimer. A qualification would understate the effect on the audit as a whole.

q: An audit team documents that no exceptions were noted in a control test but does not record which items were tested. Under SA 230 the primary deficiency is that:
o: The specific items tested are not identified, so work cannot be redone
A conclusion of no exceptions is not a valid audit conclusion at all
The working paper should have been signed by the client finance head too
The working paper does not carry a cross reference to materiality
why: SA 230 requires recording the identifying characteristics of the items tested so the work is traceable and re-performable. Without them an experienced auditor cannot evaluate whether the conclusion is supported.

q: Which of the following would ordinarily NOT need to be retained in the audit documentation?
o: Significant matters discussed with management, and when and with whom held
The basis for the conclusion on the reasonableness of an estimate
Superseded drafts and duplicate copies replaced by corrected versions
Documentation of discussions on significant matters with governance
why: Superseded drafts and duplicates replaced by corrected versions may be removed during assembly since they do not evidence the final conclusions. The other items are precisely the significant matters SA 230 requires to be documented and retained.

q: The auditor concludes that an accounting estimate is reasonable but the documentation records only the final number agreed with management. This fails SA 230 because it does not record:
o: The audit fee attributable to the work performed on the estimate
The prior year comparative amount recorded for the very same estimate
The names of every member of the engagement team involved in it
The professional judgements made and the basis for the conclusion
why: Where significant professional judgement is exercised, SA 230 requires documentation of the judgement and its basis so the reasoning is auditable. Recording only the agreed figure leaves the judgement invisible.

q: A representation from management about the completeness of related party relationships and transactions is required because:
o: It removes the auditor responsibility to search for undisclosed relations
Management holds the knowledge, but the representation supplements work
SA 550 permits sole reliance on representations for related parties
The Companies Act 2013 requires it to be obtained in place of testing
why: Management holds the primary knowledge of related parties, so a representation is required, but it complements procedures such as reviewing registers, minutes and confirmations. Treating it as a substitute would leave undisclosed relationships undetected.

q: If management provides a written representation that the auditor concludes is not reliable, SA 580 requires the auditor to:
o: Accept the representation but place reduced reliance upon it
Request a second representation signed by those charged with governance
Take action, including assessing the effect on the audit opinion
Report the matter to the Registrar of Companies without any delay
why: Doubt about integrity or reliability of a representation casts doubt on other representations and evidence generally, and may require modification of the opinion. Simply obtaining a second signature does not address the underlying reliability concern.

q: SA 230 requires documentation of discussions of significant matters. The record should include:
o: The nature of the matters, and the timing and the participants involved
Only the final conclusion that the engagement team reached on the matter
A verbatim transcript of the whole discussion as it actually occurred
The commercial impact on the client of the matter that was discussed
why: The standard calls for the nature of the matters, and the timing and participants of the discussion, so the audit trail is complete. A verbatim transcript is neither required nor practical.

q: Which document is LEAST likely to be considered audit documentation under SA 230?
o: Checklists and analyses prepared by members of the engagement team
Abstracts of significant contracts obtained by the audit team
Letters of confirmation received directly from third parties
The entity accounting records and underlying source documents
why: The entity accounting records and underlying source documents are audit evidence held by the client, not the auditor documentation, though copies or abstracts placed on file become documentation. The other three are classic examples of working papers.

q: Where the auditor departs from a relevant requirement of an SA, SA 230 requires documentation of:
o: The departure alone, since alternative procedures are a judgement matter
The reasons for departure and how alternatives achieved the aim
Approval obtained from the Institute for departing from the requirement
A modification of the auditor report describing the departure made
why: The documentation must show the reasons for departure and how the alternative procedures met the objective of the requirement. No external approval is needed, and a departure handled this way does not by itself trigger a report modification.

q: A written representation about managements intention to hold an investment to maturity is MOST usefully corroborated by:
o: A second representation obtained from the entity audit committee
A confirmation of the current market value obtained from the broker
Past practice, board minutes, forecasts and the ability to hold
The professional judgement of the engagement partner on its own
why: Intent representations require corroboration through history of similar holdings, documented board decisions, and the financial ability to hold. Market value confirmation addresses measurement, not intention.

q: The auditor documents the identifying characteristics of items tested for a purchase order sample. An acceptable identifying characteristic would be:
o: All of the purchase orders included within the selected sample
A representative selection of purchase orders raised in the year
Approximately sixty purchase orders selected from across the year
Purchase orders PO 4501 to PO 4560 raised between April and June
why: Identifying characteristics must let another auditor locate the same items, which specific document numbers and dates achieve. Vague descriptions such as representative or approximately sixty give no way to reperform the test.
